sentences.text:
This appeal was filed under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 seeking enhancement of compensation from Rs.12,00,000/-
Rs.12,00,000/ to Rs.15,95,000/-,, aggrieved by the award dated 08.01.2001 in M.O.P.No.1422 of 1999 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal-cum-II II Additional District Judge,
Visakhapatnam.
02.

entities.text:
Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal-cum-II II Additional District Judge,
Visakhapatnam
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The claim petition was filed by the legal representatives of late Sadi Suribabu who died of the injuries suffered by him in a motor vehicle accident occurred on 12.04.1999.

After adjudicating the matter, BSB,J the Claims Tribunal computed the amount of compensation at Rs.15,95,000/-,
however, the amount granted was limited to Rs.12,00,000/- as sought by the claimants in the claim petition.
Aggrieved by the same, this appeal was preferred.

03. The learned counsel for the appellants, who are the claimants before the Tribunal, submitted that the amount of compensation should be just and reasonable, irrespective of amount claimed by the petitioners and therefore the Tribunal ought to have granted Rs.15,95,000/- instead of limiting amount payable to Rs.12,00,000/- which was mentioned in the petition.

sentences.text:
On the other hand, the learned counsel for the 2 nd respondent submitted that the appeal preferred by the 2 nd respondent herein vide C.M.A.No.838 of 2001 had been decided by the Division Bench on 03.07.2007 by upholding the amount of Rs.12,00,000/-, but, reducing the rate of interest from 12% to 9% and that the appeal had been decided on merits after hearing both the parties and therefore, he requested to dispose of this appeal in terms of the order passed in that appeal.
05.

In reply, the learned counsel for the appellants submitted that the question of quantum of compensation payable to the claimants beyond the amount sought was not decided in the appeal in C.M.A.No.838 of 2001 and that the question is still debatable in the present appeal.
06. In C.M.A.No.838 of 2001, the 2nd respondent herein contended that the amount of Rs.12,00,000/- awarded is high.
Though the Tribunal calculated the compensation payable at Rs.15,95,000/-, since it awarded only Rs.12,00,000/-, the Division Bench held that it was not BSB,J high.
The question as to whether Rs.15,95,000/- is high or not was not decided.
07. A perusal of the impugned judgment, in the light of the evidence on record, shows that the amount of compensation of Rs.15,95,000/- is not on high side as it was calculated as per the evidence.
08. Since it is settled law that irrespective of the amount of compensation claimed, just and reasonable amount of compensation shall be paid.
Though the Tribunal calculated the amount of compensation payable is Rs.15,95,000/-, limited the amount of compensation awarded to Rs.12,00,000/- which was claimed.
Since it is against settled principle of law, the award is liable to be modified by raising the amount of compensation from Rs.12,00,000/- to Rs.15,95,000/-.
As the rate of interest has been reduced from 12% p.a., to 9% p.a., in C.M.A.No.838 of 2001, the same is applicable.

09. Accordingly, this appeal is allowed with proportionate costs throughout, subject to the payment of the court fee on Rs.3,95,000/- within one month from the date of receipt of the copy of this judgment.
As a sequel thereto, the miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending in this appeal shall stand closed.

JUSTICE B.S.BHANUMATHI Date: 04.09.2025 GRL BSB,J HON'BLE Ms. JUSTICE B.S.BHANUMATHI Date: 04.09.2025 GRL S.Narasayamma vs M Nookaraju And Anr on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/81961838/
